level: Cultivation Technician I / entry occupational pathway
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the THC Cultivation Technician I pathway
Entry-level cultivation employees developing supervised operational competency
evidencePolicy: Use canonical evidence-backed science and operational references for durable principles. Facility SOPs, product labels, equipment manuals, and jurisdiction-specific requirements control when they are more specific. Reused curriculum modules are development dependencies and do not substitute for course-specific occupational review.
assessmentPolicy: This owner-approved public academic course uses course-specific formative and summative/readiness evidence derived from material taught in the course. Academic course completion is educational evidence only and does not authorize professional credential issuance. Secure credential examinations, validated practical/capstone decisions, evaluator calibration, standard setting, privacy/security approval, and final credential release remain separately fail-closed.
title: Environmental, Light & Sensor Fundamentals
description: Builds entry-level skill in reading cultivation environmental and light measurements, preserving sensor context, recognizing obvious alarms or suspect readings, completing permitted verification steps, and escalating rather than independently redesigning control strategy.
learningOutcomes: Read and record temperature, relative humidity, VPD, photoperiod and PPFD with correct units, time, location and sensor context.
Use repeatable canopy measurement methods and preserve spatial light distribution rather than substituting one point or fixture setting for crop-level evidence.
Recognize suspect or non-representative environmental readings by checking placement, comparison data, verification status and trend context.
Perform only authorized operator-level checks and create reconstructable alarm, verification and shift-handoff records for unresolved environmental or lighting conditions.
